errors.text: The proposed intervention is generic high-entropy mixing rather than controlled chemical short-range ordering in an initially random bcc HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The predicted direction is opposite to the target result: the hypothesis predicts reduced conductivity, whereas SRO produces an approximately 12% increase.
The proposed disorder-scattering mechanism omits the target mechanisms of reduced lattice distortion, B2-like HfTi/TiZr clustering, and conductive percolation pathways.
The baseline changes alloy composition and complexity by comparing HEAs with low-alloy or pure-element materials, rather than comparing otherwise equivalent random and SRO states.
The experiment measures total thermal conductivity without a robust plan to separate lattice and electronic contributions, so it cannot cleanly test phonon conductivity.
The stated condition 'room temperature and below' conflicts with the stated boundary of 30–750 K.
